project_summary: The City of Riverbend is soliciting proposals for a cloud-based Online Permitting and Inspection Management System. This project aims to replace a legacy, paper-intensive process for handling approximately 6,200 annual permit applications across various categories. The selected vendor will design, implement, and support a system featuring an applicant portal, internal workflow engine, payment processing, and reporting dashboard, with optional mobile inspection and GIS integration.

evaluation_criteria: Technical Approach & Functional Fit (D1-D4): Evaluation of the proposed technical solution and its alignment with mandatory deliverables.

Vendor Qualifications & Past Performance: Assessment of vendor's experience, particularly with similar government/public-sector contracts. Proposers must demonstrate at least 3 comparable public-sector engagements completed in the last 5 years.
Cost & Total Cost of Ownership: Analysis of proposed costs, including one-time implementation and recurring annual fees.
Implementation Timeline & Project Plan Feasibility: Review of the proposed project timeline and plan for feasibility and adherence to target milestones.
Security, Data Privacy & Compliance Posture: Evaluation of the vendor's security measures, data privacy practices, and regulatory compliance.
Optional Value-Adds (D5, D6): Assessment of optional deliverables for additional value to the City.

Legal: Carry Commercial General Liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence, naming the City as additional insured.
Carry Cyber Liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence, naming the City as additional insured.
Agree to the City’s standard indemnification clause (Attachment C) without modification.
Comply with the City’s Data Privacy and Breach Notification Ordinance (Municipal Code § 14-220).
Be willing to execute a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) consistent with applicable state privacy law.
Disclose any subcontractors who will have access to City data, ensuring they meet the same security and insurance requirements as the prime vendor.
Certify compliance with the City’s Equal Employment Opportunity and Living Wage Ordinance for any locally performed labor.
Be registered and in good standing in the State of Anystate.
Ensure system hosting infrastructure is located within the continental United States (data residency).
Accounting: Adhere to standard City payment terms (Net 45).
Ensure no payment is made prior to acceptance testing sign-off for each deliverable milestone.
Provide pricing firm for the full initial 3-year term.
Cap price escalation in renewal years at 3% annually or CPI, whichever is lower.
Provide a current W-9 within 5 business days of award.
Provide a Certificate of Insurance within 5 business days of award.
Provide a Performance Bond equal to 50% of the first-year contract value prior to contract execution.
Technical: System must be cloud-hosted (SaaS or City-approved private cloud).
System must provide a 99.5% uptime SLA, measured monthly, excluding scheduled maintenance windows.
System must support Single Sign-On (SSO) via SAML 2.0 integration with the City’s existing Azure AD environment.
All data must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher).
Provide a documented disaster recovery plan with a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 4 hours or less and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 1 hour or less.
System must provide a documented, versioned REST or GraphQL API for future integrations.
Conduct a third-party penetration test prior to go-live and annually thereafter, at vendor’s expense, with results provided to the City.
System must be hosted on infrastructure located within the continental United States (data residency outside the U.S. is not permitted).
Implement technical capabilities for notification of any data breach within 24 hours of discovery, as per City ordinance.
Operations: Ensure subcontractor compliance with security and insurance requirements.
Ensure acceptance testing sign-off for each deliverable milestone prior to payment.
Implement and manage the documented disaster recovery plan to meet RTO and RPO requirements.
Coordinate and manage annual third-party penetration tests.
Establish and follow processes for notification of any data breach within 24 hours of discovery, as per City ordinance.
HR: Certify compliance with the City’s Equal Employment Opportunity and Living Wage Ordinance for any locally performed labor.

sample_rfp_city_permitting_system (1).pd:
CITY OF RIVERBEND, ANYSTATE — DEPARTMENT OF PERMITTING & DEVELOPMENT SERVICES
REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) No. 2026-PD-014
Online Permitting & Inspection Management System
Issue Date: July 1, 2026   |   Submission Deadline: August 10, 2026, 5:00 PM Local Time
Pre-Proposal Conference (Virtual): July 15, 2026, 10:00 AM Local Time
Question Submission Deadline: July 22, 2026, 5:00 PM Local Time
1. INTRODUCTION & BACKGROUND
The City of Riverbend ("the City") is seeking proposals from qualified vendors to design, implement, and
support a cloud-based Online Permitting & Inspection Management System to replace its legacy,
paper-intensive permitting process. The Department of Permitting & Development Services processes
approximately 6,200 permit applications per year across building, electrical, plumbing, and zoning
categories.
The City intends to award a single contract for an initial three (3) year term, with two optional one-year
renewals at the City's sole discretion.
2. SCOPE OF WORK — REQUIRED DELIVERABLES
Proposers must address each deliverable below. Deliverables D1–D4 are MANDATORY. Deliverables D5
and D6 are OPTIONAL value-adds and will be scored separately.
•
D1 — Online Applicant Portal (MANDATORY): Public-facing web portal allowing applicants to submit
permit applications online, upload supporting documents, track application status in real time, and pay
fees. Portal must be mobile-responsive and meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Estimated
effort: 8 weeks.
•
D2 — Internal Workflow & Review Engine (MANDATORY): Configurable, rules-based routing engine
supporting parallel and sequential review workflows across departments (Building, Fire, Zoning, Public
Works), automated SLA tracking, escalation alerts, and role-based access control. Estimated effort: 8
weeks.
•
D3 — Payment Processing Integration (MANDATORY): PCI-DSS compliant payment gateway
integration supporting credit card, ACH, and e-check payments, automated fee calculation based on
permit type/valuation, and refund processing. Estimated effort: 4 weeks.
•
D4 — Reporting & Analytics Dashboard (MANDATORY): Real-time dashboard for department heads
showing permit volume, average turnaround time, and process bottlenecks, with exportable reports
(CSV/PDF) and migration of approximately 9 years of historical permit records from the legacy system.
Estimated effort: 6 weeks.
•
D5 — Mobile Inspector App (OPTIONAL): Native or hybrid mobile application for field inspectors to log
inspection results offline, sync automatically when reconnected, with GPS tagging and photo attachment
capability. Estimated effort: 10 weeks.
•
D6 — GIS / Parcel Mapping Integration (OPTIONAL): Integration with the City's existing ArcGIS
parcel database to auto-populate property information upon application submission. Estimated effort: 8
weeks.
3. PROPOSAL EVALUATION CRITERIA
Proposals will be scored by an evaluation committee using the following weighted criteria:
•
Technical Approach & Functional Fit (D1–D4) — 35%: Evaluation of the proposed technical solution
and its alignment with mandatory deliverables.
•
Vendor Qualifications & Past Performance — 20%: Assessment of vendor's experience, particularly
with similar government/public-sector contracts. Proposers must demonstrate at least 3 comparable
public-sector engagements completed in the last 5 years.
•
Cost / Total Cost of Ownership — 20%: Analysis of proposed costs, including one-time
implementation and recurring annual fees.
•
Implementation Timeline & Project Plan Feasibility — 10%: Review of the proposed project timeline
and plan for feasibility and adherence to target milestones.
•
Security, Data Privacy & Compliance Posture — 10%: Evaluation of the vendor's security measures,
data privacy practices, and regulatory compliance.
•
Optional Value-Adds (D5, D6) — 5%: Assessment of optional deliverables for additional value to the
City.
4. LEGAL & INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS
•
Vendor must carry Commercial General Liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence AND
Cyber Liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence, naming the City as additional insured.
•
Vendor must agree to the City's standard indemnification clause (Attachment C) without modification.
•
Vendor must comply with the City's Data Privacy and Breach Notification Ordinance (Municipal Code §
14-220), including notification of any data breach within 24 hours of discovery.
•
Vendor must be willing to execute a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) consistent with applicable state
privacy law.
•
Vendor must disclose any subcontractors who will have access to City data; subcontractors are subject
to the same security and insurance requirements as the prime vendor.
•
Contract is subject to City Council approval and annual appropriation of funds (a standard
non-appropriation clause applies).
•
Vendor must certify compliance with the City's Equal Employment Opportunity and Living Wage
Ordinance for any locally performed labor.
5. ACCOUNTING & FINANCIAL REQUIREMENTS
•
Standard City payment terms are Net 45; no payment will be made prior to acceptance testing sign-off
for each deliverable milestone.
•
Proposal must include a detailed, itemized cost breakdown: one-time implementation costs, recurring
annual subscription/license/hosting costs, and any optional module costs (D5, D6) priced separately.
•
Vendor must provide pricing firm for the full initial 3-year term; price escalation in renewal years is
capped at 3% annually or CPI, whichever is lower.
•
Vendor must be registered and in good standing in the State of Anystate, and able to provide a current
W-9 and Certificate of Insurance within 5 business days of award.
•
Vendor must disclose annual revenue and provide its 2 most recent audited financial statements (or
equivalent), demonstrating sufficient financial stability to support a multi-year public sector contract of
this scope (estimated total contract value: $0.85M–$1.2M).
6. TECHNICAL & SECURITY STANDARDS
•
System must be cloud-hosted (SaaS or City-approved private cloud); on-premise solutions will not be
considered.
•
System must provide a 99.5% uptime SLA, measured monthly, excluding scheduled maintenance
windows.
•
System must support Single Sign-On (SSO) via SAML 2.0 integration with the City's existing Azure AD
environment.
•
All data must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher).
•
Vendor must provide a documented disaster recovery plan with a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 4
hours or less and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 1 hour or less.
•
System must provide a documented, versioned REST or GraphQL API for future integrations.
•
Vendor must conduct a third-party penetration test prior to go-live and annually thereafter, at vendor's
expense, with results provided to the City.
•
System must be hosted on infrastructure located within the continental United States; data residency
outside the U.S. is not permitted.
7. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS
•
Proposals must be submitted electronically via the City's eProcurement portal by the deadline stated on
the cover page (August 10, 2026, 5:00 PM Local Time). Late submissions will not be considered.
•
Proposal must not exceed 40 pages in length (excluding resumes and financial statements).
•
Proposal must include signed Attachment A (Vendor Certification), Attachment B (References —
minimum of 3 public-sector references), and Attachment C (Indemnification Acknowledgment).
•
A Performance Bond equal to 50% of the first-year contract value is required from the awarded vendor
prior to contract execution.
8. KEY DATES SUMMARY
•
Issue Date: July 1, 2026
•
Pre-Proposal Conference: July 15, 2026, 10:00 AM Local Time (virtual)
•
Question Submission Deadline: July 22, 2026, 5:00 PM Local Time
•
Proposal Submission Deadline: August 10, 2026, 5:00 PM Local Time
•
Anticipated Contract Award: September 15, 2026
•
Anticipated Project Kickoff: October 1, 2026
•
Estimated Total Budget: $0.85M–$1.2M over the initial 3-year term
